CRIMINAL APPEAL No . 65 of 2008
The Judgment was delivered by : A. K. Patnaik, J.
1.  This is an appeal by way of special leave under Article 136 of the Constitution of India against the judgment and order dated 06.02.2007 of the Allahabad High Court in Criminal Appeal No.178 of 1981.

facts: On September 22, 1979, at 8:05 pm, Balbir Singh lodged an FIR with Police Chowki Dhata, P.S. Khakhreru in District Fatehpur.

The prosecution story as stated in the FIR was that on September 22, 1979, the complainant was returning home after purchasing crude oil from Khaga and Raja Ram Singh (his father) and Kunj Behari Singh were waiting for him at Dhata and he left the oil at Dhata and the three sat on the Motorcycle No. UTY 3213.

Kunj Behari Singh drove the motorcycle and when they reached near bamboo clumps ahead of Kanya Pathshala on Dhata-Hinauta Road at about 6:00 P.M., Hira Pandey, Subhash Pandey @ Bodhan and Surendra Nath Pandey, the three appellants herein, who were waiting with single barrel gun, double barrel gun and rifle respectively and cartridge belts, started firing at them.

As soon as Kunj Behari was shot, the Motorcycle lost balance and he and his father jumped off from the bike and while his father ran towards the west into the paddy fields, he ran towards Harijan Basti.

From Dhata end, Sunder Lal Singh, Hari Prasad Singh, Lakhpat Sonar and Shisuvir Narain were coming and many other persons were coming from Kabraha side and on their exhortation, the appellants ran away to hide in the fields.
issues: Whether the trial court and High Court erred in relying on the evidence of PW-1 and PW-2.
Whether the prosecution case was weakened by the non-examination of Sunder Lal Singh and other witnesses named in the FIR.
Whether the trial court and High Court correctly believed the two eyewitnesses PW-1 and PW-2 considering the motive of the appellants to take revenge against the complainant and his father.
petitioner_arguments: The trial court and High Court should not have relied on the evidence of PW-1 as admittedly he had previous enmity with the appellants.

If PW-1 was the prime target of the appellants, he would have received some injury as according to PW-1 all the appellants were armed with fire arms and cartridges, but as a matter of fact PW-1 has not received a single injury and this would go to show that PW-1 has falsely implicated the appellants.

According to the evidence of PW-1, as soon as the motorcycle lost balance he jumped off from the motorcycle and ran away from the place of occurrence towards the Harijan Basti and therefore he could not have seen the appellant firing on the two deceased persons.
respondent_arguments: The presence of PW-1 at the spot of occurrence is supported by three circumstances: (a) that his motorcycle was found lying at the spot; (b) that his pant was torn; (c) DW-1 admitted to have seen the motorcycle lying on the western side of the road.

PW-2 could not be treated as a chance witness as the incident took place on the road and only passers-by on the road would be witnesses to any such incident which took place on the road and their evidence could not be brushed aside on the ground that they are chance witnesses.
court_reasoning: The trial court and High Court have rightly believed the two eyewitnesses PW-1 and PW-2 considering the fact that the motive of the appellants was to take revenge against the complainant and his father for not agreeing to compromise the complaint case under Sections 323, 325 and 147 of the IPC pending before the court.
holding: The conviction and sentence of the appellants are upheld.
